newsitem.title: USA: Shape of Korea talks table first 'big deal'.
newsitem.headline: Shape of Korea talks table first 'big deal'.

text.p: The quirky but sensitive issue of the shape of the negotiating table for this week's U.S.-South Korea meeting with North Korea has been finalised -- "more triangular than circular."
As is often the case with peace talks, mundane arrangements loom large in a sensitive political context.

And a senior U.S. official privy to the discussions said on Monday the shape of the table to be used at Wednesday's briefing at the Hilton Hotel in New York City was a "big deal" that was negotiated, along with some related issues, over the course of several days.

The U.S., South Korean and North Korean delegations will sit at separate tables "more or less in a triangular shape," said the official, who briefed reporters on condition of anonymity. "It's more triangular than circular."

Laborious negotiations on table shape, seating arrangements and such also accompanied such momentous negotiations as the Paris peace talks to end the Vietnam War and the 1991 Madrid peace conference that launched direct peace talks between Israel and several of its enemies, the Palestinians, Syria and Lebanon.
